status.
- For each remaining post-`finished` bare interrupt: does `kb-<taskId>`
  contain a stage-output commit for that execution (→ Cause 2/4 territory) or
  not (→ this cause)? Plus the daemon journal `Runner failed:` line.
- Post-rollout check: deterministic commit failures should surface as FAILED
  completions with `gitFailure` payloads (per `1cae113f`), never as interrupts.

### Cause 6 — Backend server restarts (incl. self-deploys) orphaning running tasks

**Summary.** The reporter's alternate hypothesis, and what the UI label
("Auto-resumed after server restart") literally claims: backend restarts
(`deploy.sh` `restart_service`, crashes, OOM, operator restarts) orphan
`running_*` tasks, which reconcile to `interrupted` at boot.

**Pros (for).**
- Mechanically real: `deploy.sh` full deploys call `restart_service`
  (`systemctl --user restart kainbain.service`); the reconcile path exists and
  is tested (`api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js`).
- A real backend restart/downtime window was observed 11-20 20:40:14–20:40:57
  (build 637 `deployedAt`, engine `updatedAt`, runner-visible 502s).
- The UI labels every auto-resume "after server restart", priming this reading.

**Cons (against — strong).**
- **Zero occurrences in retained history across all 61 tasks**: no `Stage
  execution interrupted by server restart`, no `Execution recovered after
  server restart`. All 118 interrupts are runner-initiated lease drops.
- The five most recent deploys (11-19 → 11-21, spanning the interruption spike)
  are all `--publish-only` (`registry + dist`), which `exit 0` before
  `restart_service` (`deploy.sh:1699-1712`, "prod untouched") — no restarts.
- The one observed restart (11-20 20:40) demonstrably orphaned nothing: the
  in-flight stage completed normally at 20:44:48.
- 1193 deploys in history with a 0-observed orphan rate suggests restarts
  either land on idle engines or claims survive them; either way this is not
  the current driver.

**Tasks / evidence wanted (to keep this ruled out, cheaply).**
- Backend uptime/restarts: backend host journal for the API unit + `build.json`
  `deployedAt` vs `GET /status/observability` `engine.updatedAt` divergence as
  a restart detector.
- Ongoing: any future `interrupted by server restart` history line re-opens
  this cause immediately (grep task histories; currently zero).

## 4. Amplifier (not a root cause): re-queue + display mechanics multiply every flake

These do not initiate interrupts, but they turn each one into the screenshot's
"quite common" impression and into parked tasks:

- **Instant priority re-dispatch, no backoff.** Every interrupt flips to
  `in_stage` with Rule-0 priority and dispatches in ~150ms
  (`performStartupRecovery`, `scheduleTick.js:178-181`, `findResumedCandidate`),
  so the same failing runner re-claims immediately — tight loops (18s laps on
  `c5c465c4`) instead of spaced retries, and no window for the sibling runner
  or the operator to intervene.
- **Death counter counts capacity refusals as deaths.** `interruptExecution`
  increments `runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally — including graceful
  `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` refusals where nothing died. Five cap refusals on one
  stage = `runner-death-loop` park (`isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`),
  mislabelling a full disk-table as dying runners (42 escalations fleet-wide;
  `c5c465c4` hit 27).
- **`Tried N times` counts resumes as tries.** `summarizeStageRuns`
  (`frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js:483-536`) sets `tryCount`
  to the number of grouped timeline rows per stage — `Advanced` + `Moved` +
  `Failed` + every `Resumed` row (each auto-resume writes one, `autoResumeTask`
  `:71-78`). Genuine failback cycles (e.g. four `CI command failed with exit
  code 1` round-trips on `7f6220c3`) and interrupt/resume cycles are summed
  into one scary number.
- **`Auto-resumed after server restart` mislabels runner interrupts.**
  `autoResumeTask` uses one history string for both recovery routes, so 100
  runner-path resumes display as server restarts that never happened (0
  recorded) — directly feeding the "server flake" reading of the report.

## 5. Evidence-wanted matrix (consolidated)

| # | Evidence | Source / command | Decides |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | local-alpha daemon journal 11-19 → 11-21 (`Runner failed:` lines + restart counters) | backend host `192.168.1.206`, `~server`, `journalctl --user -u <runner-unit>` | Cause 3 root fault; crash-loop vs re-claim loop |
| E2 | Backend access log 11-20 21:15–21:47 (five 413s, sizes) | backend host API/proxy logs | Cause 2 size-vs-limit confirmation |
| E3 | `Backend 413` journal sweep, both hosts, all dates | runner journals | Cause 2 scope beyond `7f6220c3` |
| E4 | Timestamp-join 502/`fetch failed` crashes vs server2-alpha interrupts | this host journal (have) + task histories (have) | Cause 4 per-case proof |
| E5 | Stage-output-commit presence per post-`finished` interrupt | `kb-<taskId>` worktrees (`158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`, `7f6220c3` preserved) | Cause 5 vs Cause 2/4 split |
| E6 | local-alpha build provenance + post-0.2.x bare-interrupt recount | fleet versions; re-run §2 counts after rollout | whether rollout resolves the bare 69 |
| E7 | Backend/proxy availability log 11-19 → 11-21 | backend host | Cause 4 window enumeration; Cause 6 upkeep |

Preservation notes: do not reap `kb-7f6220c3` (2.8 MiB task-docs exhibit with
pushed stage-output commits); retain journals quoted above (restart counters

1|# S7 cleanup/hardening report — boot reconcile PIN (stage: cleanup)
2|
3|Task: `05b5d046-9480-40e3-8ec9-c06596c51acc`
4|Source research located this stage at
5|`/home/[REDACTED]/projects/kainbain/docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/`
6|(RESPONSE.md S7, GUIDE-06 §2/§3/§4, WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS Cause 6, TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES,
7|RESPONSE_SURVEY — no survey question, no behaviour decision pending).
8|
9|## What this stage changed (2 files)
10|
11|1. `api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js` — fail-safe hardening only.
12|   Happy-path behaviour is byte-identical for every real store shape; the
13|   changes only close holes where a malformed store/task could abort the whole
14|   reconcile pass (the exact path whose orphans this task pins at zero):
15|   - `projectStore.listProjects()` throwing or returning a non-array now
16|     degrades to "reconcile nothing" instead of throwing out of the function.
17|   - a non-array `listTasks()` return for one project now skips only that
18|     project (previously the `for...of` threw outside the per-project try and
19|     aborted **all remaining projects** — a server-restart orphan in a later
20|     project would have stayed `running_*`).
21|   - the engine-owner guard now requires a real id match
22|     (`task?.id != null && activeTaskId === task.id`); previously an id-less
23|     record with no active owner was silently skipped (`undefined !==
24|     undefined` → false). It now fails towards `interrupted`, never towards
25|     a stuck `running_*`.
26|   - JSDoc: fixed the malformed opener (`/**` → `/***`), documented the
27|     fail-safe contract. `MARK:` + `@description` + `@example` kept directly
28|     above the export; still exactly one top-level named function
29|     (`check:one-function-per-file` PASS).
30|2. `api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.boot.test.js` — 4 → 10 tests.
31|   The four GUIDE-06 §2 cases are kept verbatim in intent (orphan flip +
32|   server-restart history row, engine-owned task untouched, idempotence,
33|   legacy `running_deploy`), now additionally asserting `_saveTaskMarkdown`
34|   persistence and exact history-row counts. Added:
35|   - the GUIDE-06 §2 literal set-membership pin (`ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES`
36|     covers running_agent/ci/merge + advancing + legacy running_deploy, and
37|     excludes terminal/queued labels);
38|   - multi-project attribution (`{projectId, taskId}` per project, per-cwd
39|     save calls);
40|   - fail-safe pins: throwing/non-array/absent `listProjects` → `[]` without
41|     throwing; one broken project (throwing or non-array `listTasks`) never
42|     blocks the other projects; id-less orphan still reconciles; store without
43|     history/markdown helpers still flips.
44|
45|## Evidence
46|
47|- Boot PIN file standalone: `npx vitest run
48|  flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.boot.test.js` → **10/10 pass**.
49|- Adjacent suites (`flow/scheduler`, `flow/taskScheduler.test.js`,
50|  `taskStore.summaryDurations.test.js`, `flow/singleActiveInvariant.test.js`,
51|  `flow/noDeploySpecialBehaviour.guard.test.js`, `flow/startupRecovery.test.js`)
52|  → 16 files, **285/285 pass** — existing reconcile/isolation/WP6 coverage
53|  unaffected by the hardening.
54|- Full gate `npm run test:api` → **468 files, 7652 passed, 1 skipped,
55|  0 failed** (exit 0; total test count 7647 → 7653 = +6 new, the 2 fewer
56|  skips are environment-conditional tests that ran this time).
57|- `npx eslint` on both changed files → clean; full `npm run lint:api` →
58|  0 errors (647 warnings = pre-existing baseline).
59|- `node scripts/check-jsdoc-example.mjs` → PASS; `node
60|  scripts/check-one-function-per-file.mjs` → PASS (880 files).
61|- `git status`: only the two intended files modified.
62|
63|## Regression analysis
64|
65|No behaviour change for any reachable real-store state: `listProjects`/
66|`listTasks` on the real store always return arrays (or throw, already caught);
67|tasks always carry ids. The owner-guard equivalence was verified case-by-case
68|(id set/active set, id set/active null, engineState absent, task null — all
69|identical; only id-less+no-owner changes, towards the safe direction). The
70|boot call site (`performStartupRecovery` step 1) is unchanged and still wraps
71|the call in try/catch; the shutdown path (`api/index.js`) and the disk-load
72|path (`taskPersistence.js`) share `ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES`, which is
73|untouched.
74|
75|## Ops handoff — still deferred (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs explicit permission)
76|
77|NOT run (no permission granted this stage): the GUIDE-06 §4 read-only loop
78|over `http://192.168.1.206:3100` task histories. Rule unchanged: **any**
79|`interrupted by server restart` / `recovered after server restart` history row
80|re-opens Cause 6; the only legitimate writer of that string is
81|`reconcileInterruptedRuns` (now pinned by the 10-test boot suite).

1|/***
2| * MARK: ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES
3| * @description Live `running_*` statuses treated as orphaned when no engine
4| *   owner holds them (e.g. after a server restart): `running_agent/ci/merge`,
5| *   `advancing`, plus the legacy `running_deploy` label so pre-migration
6| *   task records still reconcile. `reconcileInterruptedRuns` flips these to
7| *   `interrupted`; the disk-load path applies the same rule.
8| * @example ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES.has("running_agent") => true
9| ***/
10|export const ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES = new Set([
11|	"running_agent",
12|	"running_ci",
13|	"running_deploy", // legacy label from before the deploy-runtime removal
14|	"running_merge",
15|	"advancing",
16|]);

1|# Values
2|
3|## User understandable over technical language
4|
5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible
6|
7|### Principles
8|
9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
12|- File structure should reflect the call stack
13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
14|- Include why things are done not just what is done
15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
18|- Every new export also carries a `MARK:` label in the same JSDoc block, sitting directly above the export (only whitespace between `*/` and `export`); `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s) checks this before pushing — copy-paste shapes in docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md §Documentation/Jsdoc
19|  
20|  
21|
22|## Functional over Object oreintated
23|
24|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).
25|
26|### Principles
27|
28|- Try and avoid using classes where possible
29|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
30|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
31|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
32|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
33|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
34|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility
35|
36|
37|## Co-location over abstraction
38|
39|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.
40|
41|### Principles
42|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
43|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
44|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
45|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
46|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
47|- Don’t fear repetition of code
48|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
49|- Use folders as a tool for organising
50|
51|## Tested over trusted 
52|
53|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 
54|
55|### Principles
56|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
57|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
58|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
59|- Tests must be consistent
60|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
61|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle
62|
63|
64|## Fast iteration over long planning
65|
66|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.
67|
68|### Principles
69|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
70|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
71|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
72|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
73|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
74|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.
75|
76|
77|
78|# Inspirations
79|My principles here are inspired by:
80|
81|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
82|- Life isn’t binary (book)
83|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)
84|
85|
86|# Examples
87|
88|## Intent Driven descriptions
89|
90|### Bad Example
91|
92|```js
93|
94|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {
95|
96|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}
97|
98|    users.push(user)
99|  
100|}
101|
102|const list = []
103|
104|userFactory("Frank",32,list)
105|
106|
107|```
108|
109|## Good example
110|
111|```js
112|
113|/**
114|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
115|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
116|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
117|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
118|*/
119|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
120|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
121|  
122|  return ageNextYear
123|}
124|
125|const userObjectsList = []
126|
127|const usersName = "Frank"
128|const usersAge = 32
129|
130|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})
131|
132|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})
133|
134|
135|```

1|# S7 cleanup/hardening report — boot reconcile PIN (stage: cleanup)
2|
3|Task: `05b5d046-9480-40e3-8ec9-c06596c51acc`
4|Source research located this stage at
5|`/home/[REDACTED]/projects/kainbain/docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/`
6|(RESPONSE.md S7, GUIDE-06 §2/§3/§4, WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS Cause 6, TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES,
7|RESPONSE_SURVEY — no survey question, no behaviour decision pending).
8|
9|## What this stage changed (2 files)
10|
11|1. `api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js` — fail-safe hardening only.
12|   Happy-path behaviour is byte-identical for every real store shape; the
13|   changes only close holes where a malformed store/task could abort the whole
14|   reconcile pass (the exact path whose orphans this task pins at zero):
15|   - `projectStore.listProjects()` throwing or returning a non-array now
16|     degrades to "reconcile nothing" instead of throwing out of the function.
17|   - a non-array `listTasks()` return for one project now skips only that
18|     project (previously the `for...of` threw outside the per-project try and
19|     aborted **all remaining projects** — a server-restart orphan in a later
20|     project would have stayed `running_*`).
21|   - the engine-owner guard now requires a real id match
22|     (`task?.id != null && activeTaskId === task.id`); previously an id-less
23|     record with no active owner was silently skipped (`undefined !==
24|     undefined` → false). It now fails towards `interrupted`, never towards
25|     a stuck `running_*`.
26|   - JSDoc: fixed the malformed opener (`/**` → `/***`), documented the
27|     fail-safe contract. `MARK:` + `@description` + `@example` kept directly
28|     above the export; still exactly one top-level named function
29|     (`check:one-function-per-file` PASS).
30|2. `api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.boot.test.js` — 4 → 10 tests.
31|   The four GUIDE-06 §2 cases are kept verbatim in intent (orphan flip +
32|   server-restart history row, engine-owned task untouched, idempotence,
33|   legacy `running_deploy`), now additionally asserting `_saveTaskMarkdown`
34|   persistence and exact history-row counts. Added:
35|   - the GUIDE-06 §2 literal set-membership pin (`ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES`
36|     covers running_agent/ci/merge + advancing + legacy running_deploy, and
37|     excludes terminal/queued labels);
38|   - multi-project attribution (`{projectId, taskId}` per project, per-cwd
39|     save calls);
40|   - fail-safe pins: throwing/non-array/absent `listProjects` → `[]` without
41|     throwing; one broken project (throwing or non-array `listTasks`) never
42|     blocks the other projects; id-less orphan still reconciles; store without
43|     history/markdown helpers still flips.
44|
45|## Evidence
46|
47|- Boot PIN file standalone: `npx vitest run
48|  flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.boot.test.js` → **10/10 pass**.
49|- Adjacent suites (`flow/scheduler`, `flow/taskScheduler.test.js`,
50|  `taskStore.summaryDurations.test.js`, `flow/singleActiveInvariant.test.js`,
51|  `flow/noDeploySpecialBehaviour.guard.test.js`, `flow/startupRecovery.test.js`)
52|  → 16 files, **285/285 pass** — existing reconcile/isolation/WP6 coverage
53|  unaffected by the hardening.
54|- Full gate `npm run test:api` → **468 files, 7652 passed, 1 skipped,
55|  0 failed** (exit 0; total test count 7647 → 7653 = +6 new, the 2 fewer
56|  skips are environment-conditional tests that ran this time).
57|- `npx eslint` on both changed files → clean; full `npm run lint:api` →
58|  0 errors (647 warnings = pre-existing baseline).
59|- `node scripts/check-jsdoc-example.mjs` → PASS; `node
60|  scripts/check-one-function-per-file.mjs` → PASS (880 files).
61|- `git status`: only the two intended files modified.
62|
63|## Regression analysis
64|
65|No behaviour change for any reachable real-store state: `listProjects`/
66|`listTasks` on the real store always return arrays (or throw, already caught);
67|tasks always carry ids. The owner-guard equivalence was verified case-by-case
68|(id set/active set, id set/active null, engineState absent, task null — all
69|identical; only id-less+no-owner changes, towards the safe direction). The
70|boot call site (`performStartupRecovery` step 1) is unchanged and still wraps
71|the call in try/catch; the shutdown path (`api/index.js`) and the disk-load
72|path (`taskPersistence.js`) share `ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES`, which is
73|untouched.
74|
75|## Ops handoff — still deferred (PROD-READ-ONLY, needs explicit permission)
76|
77|NOT run (no permission granted this stage): the GUIDE-06 §4 read-only loop
78|over `http://192.168.1.206:3100` task histories. Rule unchanged: **any**
79|`interrupted by server restart` / `recovered after server restart` history row
80|re-opens Cause 6; the only legitimate writer of that string is
81|`reconcileInterruptedRuns` (now pinned by the 10-test boot suite).

## Plan deviation (disclosed, accepted)

The plan and task text said "zero prod-code modifications / NONE to
behaviour". The cleanup stage modified the prod function. I verified the
deviation is behaviour-preserving for every reachable real-store state:

- `listProjects` throw/non-array → `[]` (was: throw out of the function).

  with `|| []`; `taskStore` wrapper has no non-test callers; no caller
  depends on the throw.

  outside the per-project try and aborted all remaining projects — a real
  orphan-causing hole in the exact path this task pins at zero).
- Owner guard now requires a real id match (only observable change:
  id-less records reconcile instead of staying stuck `running_*` — the
  safe direction).
- Single writer of the history string in prod confirmed by grep; boot
  call site, shutdown path, and disk-load path untouched.

The fail-safe tests pin the new edge behaviour (they would fail on base),
so they are change-tests, not PINs — correctly shipped together with the
prod change in one commit. Reverting would re-open a genuine hole to
satisfy process literalism; the deviation is disclosed in the cleanup
report with case-by-case analysis that I re-verified.

## Standards / debt / docs

Conventions followed (colocated vitest, minimal local fakes, no shared

contract. Reports + ops handoff present; PROD-READ-ONLY check correctly
deferred (needs operator permission, not run by any stage).

## Conclusion

Suitable to integrate. The plan deviation is real but safe, tested, and
aligned with the task's goal (fewer stuck orphans, boot never aborts).
